current_f2_observations.finding: The stronger mainline WP1207 target-host run remained QUEUED on the self-hosted route at observation time.
Trigger-4 observed 33 queued controller-repository runs and zero in-progress runs while the admitted self-hosted route was unavailable.

A redundant WP1207 branch run was cancelled after a no-op successor reused its concurrency group with cancel-in-progress=true. This is bounded evidence that queue cancellation/coalescing is operational on the current controller platform, not merely a README hypothesis.
The stronger mainline WP1207 target-host workflow has no concurrency key, so logically equivalent probe generations are not automatically coalesced with branch-specific successors.

external_primary_sources.finding: A concurrency group permits at most one running member; by default only one pending member is retained and a newer queued member replaces the prior pending member. cancel-in-progress=true can also cancel a running member. Current 2026 docs expose queue=single as the default and queue=max up to 100 pending members. Group names operate repository-wide, including across workflows.
If no matching online idle self-hosted runner exists, jobs remain queued until a runner comes online and fail after 24 hours. This explains why backlog can grow independently of probe correctness.

Buildbot can collapse compatible build requests when requests arrive faster than workers can satisfy them; it explicitly documents the tradeoff that individual results are lost. Custom collapse predicates are supported.

Milestones enforce build ordering and abort an older build that attempts to pass after a newer build already passed the milestone; this is a useful structural analogue for a pre-effect freshness gate.
GitLab can auto-cancel pending/running redundant pipelines on newer changes, with interruptibility controls for running work.
CircleCI documents automatic cancellation of non-terminated workflows when a newer pipeline is triggered on the same branch, explicitly to reduce queue delay.

Artifact provenance binds an executed output to its exact build definition, dependencies and invocation identity. This supports exact-subject evidence but does not itself solve freshness or queue prioritization.

hypothesis: For scarce F2 target-runtime probes, a repository-native latest-representative queue policy can reduce promotion-staleness debt without adding a heavyweight scheduler: use one concurrency family per semantic runtime boundary, preserve at most one pending representative, and perform an explicit subject-freshness gate before expensive/effectful execution.
counterhypotheses: A global latest-wins queue would incorrectly erase distinct workpackages or experiments; coalescing must be scoped to a semantic probe family, not repository HEAD.
cancel-in-progress=true can destroy useful exact-source evidence or interrupt a non-idempotent/effectful path; running probes should not be cancelled by default.
Queue coalescing does not repair an offline runner. It only reduces obsolete backlog while preserving one latest representative.
Commit recency alone is insufficient: unrelated commits must not invalidate a probe. The key must bind workpackage/generation or an explicit semantic subject fingerprint.
SLSA-style provenance proves what executed, not whether that subject is still promotion-representative. Freshness needs a separate witness.
